title: Deep Review Ranked Initiative
description: One row of the Phase 10 approval table. PRODUCER: Phase 10 (10-ranked.json, plus a generated .md view — the JSON is canonical). CONSUMER: TRENT. This is the pipeline's terminal artifact: Phases 0-10 end here and nothing structural executes until he approves a sequence. FILE SHAPE: the artifact is a collection.schema.json envelope whose `items` are these objects, ordered by `rank` — this schema validates one row, not the table. Every row must point at a synthesised plan, so approving a row approves a specific, adversarially-reviewed design rather than a title.

rank.description: 1-based position in the recommended order. Unique across the table. Rank is a recommendation, not a decision — Trent reorders.

initiative_id.description: Joins to plan.schema.json initiative_id and the key in 04-ledger.json `initiatives`.

title.description: The initiative's title from 04-ledger.json, verbatim. Restating it differently here would make the two artifacts disagree.

criticals.description: How many severity='critical' findings this initiative resolves, counted from the ledger. The single strongest ranking input.

estimated_loc.description: Estimated total lines changed, copied from the synthesised plan's estimated_loc. An estimate that feeds ranking, never an acceptance criterion — no row is scored on lines removed.

risk.description: The highest step risk in the synthesised plan. low = mechanical and behaviour-preserving by construction. medium = crosses module boundaries. high = touches the render loop, packages/core, or a live output path.

payoff.description: Expected reduction in interface per unit of behaviour, plus resilience gained. high = removes a whole duplicated subsystem or closes a silent-failure path. medium = meaningful surface reduction in one module. low = tidy-up worth doing when it is cheap.

depends_on.description: Initiative ids that must land first, from the plan's dependencies_on_other_initiatives. A row whose dependency ranks below it is a sequencing defect in this table.

recommended_order_reason.description: Why HERE and not elsewhere, in terms of dependency, risk and payoff. The one line that makes the ordering arguable rather than asserted.

plan_ref.description: Repo-relative path to the Phase 9 synthesised plan this row approves. Pinning the path is what makes approval concrete: a row without a surviving plan behind it is a wish.

status.description: ready = approved-eligible, no unmet dependency. blocked = cannot start (unmet dependency or an open question owned by Trent). queued = approved and waiting on capacity. executing = in flight. done = landed on committed HEAD and pushed. Execution states are out of scope for this spec and exist so the table can be reused as the tracker.

blocked_reason.description: Why this row is blocked when no initiative dependency explains it — typically an open question the plan flagged as owned by Trent.

open_questions_for_trent.description: The plan's blocking open_questions with owner='trent', surfaced here so the approval gate shows what he must decide before this row can move.

findings_resolved.description: Total ledger findings this initiative closes, criticals included. Lets the table reconcile against 04-ledger.json counts.

allOf.description: ENFORCED: a blocked row must say what blocks it — either a named dependency or a written reason. 'blocked' with neither is unactionable at the approval gate.
ENFORCED: a 'ready' row has no unmet initiative dependency. Anything with a dependency is blocked or queued until that dependency is done, which this table cannot assert on its own.
